title: Witness existence from good specifications
statement: Let $C,c	ext{ in } acks lash	extbackslash N$, let $V$ be a language of bit strings, and let $x,U$ be bit strings. Suppose that for every triple of bit strings $u',j,p$, the length bounds $|u'|=C(|x|+1)^c$, $|j|\le C(|x|+1)^c$, and $|p|\le C(|x|+1)^c$ do not hold together with any of the three bad cases: the corresponding circuit query rejects the all-ones marker; or $|p|=C(|x|+1)^c$ and the query on $0p$ accepts while $ g g x,p g$ is not in $V$; or $|j|+|p|+1=C(|x|+1)^c$, the query on $1 0 p$ preceded by $|j|$ ones accepts, and both queries on $0(p0)$ and $0(p1)$ preceded by $|j|$ ones reject. Then for every $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^c$, there is a string $v$ of that length such that $ g g x,u g,v g$ belongs to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of bit strings
No triple satisfies the length bounds and any bad-specification case
caveat: The bad-specification predicate is expanded descriptively because its circuit-query and encoding conventions are nested.
